a1-about.author: claude
a1-about.text:
# About these mockups
- A quick low-poly scene built in Blender from the references, rendered from the game camera
- **Version 3** (top row): winding paths, chunkier rocks, one-piece trunks, berries in patches, no purple clumps
- **Version 2**: the first smooth, textured ground
- **Version 1**: faceted ground
- Everything is placeholder: models, colors, effects, the HUD and names

a1-day.author: claude
a1-day.text:
# Daylight, from the references
- Tall Scots pines with orange bark higher up
- Big granite boulders with moss and pale lichen
- Needle-covered paths crossed by roots
- Blueberry, lingonberry, heather and reindeer lichen
- Still forest ponds, rune stones, Swedish signposts

a1-fog.author: claude
a1-fog.text:
# When the fog rolls in
- Cold, grey-blue and washed out
- Glowing see-through spirits, some with antlers, and a spirit stag
- Rune stones glow; lanterns and candles give warm light
- Bogs, fallen logs and dead trees

am-glance.author: claude
am-glance.text:
# Act 1 at a glance
- Seven areas traced from your act1_layout.png, at about 1.2 m per sketch unit
- **Tallmo** (town) opens onto **Storskogen**, the hub
- From Storskogen: **Härddalen** to the north-east, **Gamla gården** to the east, **Dimskogen** to the north-west
- Dimskogen leads down to **Dimmyren**, then a winding path west to **Ödeskogen**, where the act ends
- About 1.2 km² to walk; Storskogen alone is about 720 × 650 m

am-names.author: claude
am-names.text:
# Zone names (suggestions)
- **Tallmo**: the town
- **Storskogen**: the fairmeadow
- **Härddalen**: Hearthvale
- **Gamla gården**: the Old Courtyard
- **Dimskogen**: the Misty Woods
- **Dimmyren**: the Misty Swamp
- **Ödeskogen**: the Forsaken Forest

am-questions.author: claude
am-questions.text:
# Open questions
- Do the Swedish zone names work, or should some stay English?
- Should the fog stay with Dimskogen and beyond, or roll in and out anywhere?
- Is Tallmo big enough, or should it grow?
- Is 7 main and 5 side quests the right mix?
- Do the zone sizes feel right for 1–2 hours?

am-story.author: claude
am-story.text:
# Main story (placeholder)
- **1 Vägen ut:** clear the road to the crossroads
- **4 Vårdkasen:** light the beacon on the lookout hill
- **5 Den kalla härden:** find the survivors of the burned farm
- **8 Förvaltarens brev:** the steward's letter points to the fog
- **9 När dimman kommer:** follow the wisps into Dimskogen
- **11 De sjunkna stenarna:** raise the sunken rune stones
- **12 Den hornkrönte:** face the Antlered One at the dead tree

Plus 5 side quests. Main story about 80 min, everything about 1 h 55 min.

am-terrain.author: claude
am-terrain.text:
# Storskogen terrain
- Open meadows: **Stora ängen** and **Hagen**
- Dense pine and spruce: **Tätskogen**
- Raised: **Åsen**, an 11 m esker ridge with a trail on top, and **Utsiktsberget**, an 18 m lookout hill
- Lowered: **Trollgrytan**, a 10 m deep kettle hole with a grove, a tarn and a stone circle
- Steepest slope anywhere in Act 1 is 20°, so all of it is walkable

art-details.author: claude
art-details.text:
# Props and details
- **Rocks:** chunky, with uneven faces of mixed shapes and sizes, not lots of small triangles
- **Tree trunks:** one piece, straight or gently leaning
- **Paths:** winding, uneven width, curved forks, and worn into the grass: no hard edge, the grass thins out toward them. Light tan dirt, with gravel and pebbles in the same tones
- **Berries:** grouped in patches, sitting on the bushes
- **Avoid:** blocky purple flower clumps

art-ground.author: claude
art-ground.text:
# Ground vs. props
- **Ground:** a smooth, flat surface with painted textures: moss, grass patches, gravel on dirt paths, scattered fallen leaves
- **Under trees:** grass, no brown patches
- **Props** (trees, bushes, rocks): faceted low-poly shapes

bs-about.author: claude
bs-about.text:
# Trees beside the hero stay
You found a pine on the meadow still a stump with the hero well to its side, and asked why. It wasn't meant to: two things in the test for the lower middle of the screen.
- A tree counted by its whole trunk, from its foot to its top. Seen from above, a trunk leans in towards the middle of the screen as it rises, so a tall tree beside the area reached into its corner
- The trunk's thickness came from the tree's footprint near the ground, which for pines and spruces takes in their low branches: 3 to 6 m across instead of half a metre

Now a tree counts by where it stands, its foot and the first 2 m of its trunk, as thick as its stump. And with In front, only the trees at least 1 m in front of the hero go: those beside it or past it stay, unless they hide the hero or come near the camera.

bs-spot.author: claude
bs-spot.caption: Your shot (left): the pine to the left of the hero was a stump, the hero 7 m to its side. Now (right), from the same spot, it stands.

cam-control.author: claude
cam-control.text:
# Camera control
- Hold the **right mouse button** and move the mouse to orbit the camera around the hero, like in WoW
- Sideways turns the view around the hero
- Up and down changes the angle: from straight down, through the default high view, to low behind the hero

cam-means.author: claude
cam-means.text:
# What a free camera changes
- **WASD follows the camera:** W walks away from the camera, whichever way it faces
- **Right click is taken,** so attacks and skills use left click and the keyboard
- **Low angles show the horizon,** so we need a sky, distant forest and haze to hide the edge of the map
- **Trees must fade** between the camera and the hero at every angle
- **Aiming gets touchy at low angles,** where the ground is seen almost edge-on

cam-questions.author: claude
cam-questions.text:
# Open camera questions
- Zoom in and out with the mouse wheel?
- How low and how high can the camera go?
- When you let go of the right button, does the camera stay where you left it?
- Should it ever swing back behind the hero by itself?
- Does the mouse cursor hide while you rotate?

co-about.author: claude
co-about.text:
# The cone
As you drew it in camera_view: a cone from the edges of the screen to the hero, and whatever of a tree is inside it fades away. At the camera it's the whole screen, so branches never sweep in from the edges; towards the hero it narrows, ending round the hero a little bigger than it (2.5 times), so you see the ground there. Past the hero nothing fades.

- **A gradient, not a cut:** in the cone's middle trees are gone; across its outer 30% they fade gradually, in a fine dither two pixels across that reads as the needles turning see-through. No hard edges as with the x-ray
- **Spruces** no longer go whole. One fades only where it comes into the cone round the hero, more the nearer the hero, so walking in under its outer branches thins just those
- **No bare sticks:** the cone cuts no tree whole, so no trunks or stumps are left; the shadows stay

co-close.author: claude
co-close.caption: Close up, with the camera low at the start: the spruce between the camera and the hero thins out in a fine dither, more and more towards the hero, rather than in holes with hard edges.

co-high.author: claude
co-high.caption: The same with the default, high camera.

co-low.author: claude
co-low.caption: Walking the trail with the camera low: Line to hero, Front with stumps left, and the cone (now). Line and Front cut whole trees; the cone opens a soft-edged way through the trees to the hero.

co-sketch.author: claude
co-sketch.caption: Your camera_view sketch (left): the cone from the edges of the screen to the hero. Now (right), in the thicket: whatever of the trees is inside the cone fades, wholly in its middle and gradually towards its edges; the rest of the forest stands.

co-spruce.author: claude
co-spruce.caption: Walking in behind a big spruce (2.5 m past its trunk), from 7 m to its side to straight behind it. Front (top) cuts it whole while the hero is still well beside it; the cone (bottom) leaves it standing and thins only what comes round the hero.

co-switches.author: claude
co-switches.text:
# To try in F2
Under **Trees in the way**: **Cone** (now), or the earlier ways, **Front**, **X-ray**, **Area**, **Line** and **Keep**. For the cone: **soft share** (how much of it fades gradually), **round the hero** (how big it is there; smaller, and trees wait until they nearly cover the hero), **wide for longer** (it stays wide further from the camera) and **fade in** (**Dither** or **Patches**). Front now leaves stumps; bare trunks are under **leave**.

The cone runs about 2 ms a frame slower than Front at the start (about 80 fps there), as it cuts no tree whole.

fs-about.author: claude
fs-about.text:
# Faster see-through
You saw 40 fps with the camera low, looking through the thickest forest. Measured there, the cost was the see-through trees themselves: where a tree lets what's behind it through, each of its leaf cards still runs before it's thrown away, layer on layer, and with nothing in front to stop them, every see-through tree's do. 6 to 10 of them cost 5 to 8 ms a frame, more than drawing them solid or what's behind them.

Now a see-through tree is drawn near the camera with half its leaf cards per clump, and looks the same at 50%, a touch more see-through. The slowest views went from 26 to 28 ms a frame to 22; walking the trail with the camera low, the slowest 5% of frames from 38 fps to 45, the slowest 1% from 35 to 42, and the average from 72 to 76.

What's left there is the forest itself: ambient occlusion and shadows cost 3 to 4 ms each in those views, both in F2 if you'd trade some of the look for speed. Your settings are the defaults now: the hero alone, 90%, 50%. **see-through trees** in F2: Fewer cards (now) or All cards.

fs-cards.author: claude
fs-cards.caption: The three slowest low-camera views, the see-through trees with all their cards (left) and with fewer (right): 28.0 to 22.2, 27.5 to 22.2 and 25.9 to 22.1 ms a frame.

history-link.author: claude
history-link.text: Every step of this board so far, from the first sketch to the whole of Act 1: your requests, what changed, every screenshot and earlier attempt, and the notes as they read at each step.
history-link.title: Design history

hn-about.author: claude
hn-about.text:
# Hide all but nearest
Your question: would hiding some of the trees between the camera and the hero save more than keeping them see-through? Yes: a hidden tree costs nothing to draw, while a see-through one still runs its leaf cards wherever it lets through. So it's an option now (F2, **hide all but nearest**: Off, 1 or 2; off by default): deep in the forest, only the one or two see-through trees nearest the hero stay see-through, and the rest go whole over 0.15 s, leaving only their shadows, until they no longer cover the hero.

In the slowest low-camera views: 16 to 17 ms a frame instead of 22 to 24 (keeping 2, about the same). Walking the trail with the camera low, keeping 1 takes the slowest 5% of frames from 44-46 fps to 50-51, the slowest 1% from 40-43 to 46. The stipple over most of the screen goes and the hero shows clearly; but the trees in the way vanish instead of staying half there.

hn-shots.author: claude
hn-shots.caption: The slowest low-camera views: all the see-through trees kept (left), all but the nearest hidden (middle), all but the two nearest (right). The hidden trees leave their stumps.

hud-about.author: claude
hud-about.text:
# About this HUD
- Drawn as its own layer over the version 3 renders
- **Version 2** (top): hard edges, hammered iron, thin brass trim, slim orb rims
- **Version 1** (below): the smoother first pass
- Ability names and icons are placeholders
- The lettering is Cinzel, a free font under the SIL Open Font License

hud-questions.author: claude
hud-questions.text:
# Open HUD questions
- Mana, or a different resource such as rage or stamina?
- Potions or flasks on the bar?
- Numbers on the orbs all the time, or only on hover?
- How many skill slots: 5 keys plus left click, or more?

hud-style.text:
# HUD style
- Rustic Norse ARPG: hammered iron, brass, runes and knotwork
- **Sharp and detailed**, not smooth: hard edges, cut corners, fine texture
- **Red life orb** and **blue mana orb** with slim rims
- Painted, colorful ability icons
- Fantasy lettering for names and numbers

hud2-closeup.caption: Version 2 close-up: slim orb rims with clasps, an iron plate with engraved knots and bolts, and a segmented experience bar.

if-about.author: claude
if-about.text:
# Trees in front of the hero
You found that with **Lower middle** too many trees ahead were cut before the hero got close to them, and that with **Line to hero** branches, like the pine's in the top right of your shot, pop into the screen with a low camera. You asked for the best of both.

**In front**, now the default, clears what stands between the camera and the hero, and leaves what's past the hero alone:
- Trees in front of the hero in the lower middle of the screen go, to their stumps
- So does every tree whose leaves come near the camera, wherever it is on the screen, so the branches round the camera don't sweep in from its edges
- A tree gone near the camera stays gone while it's on the screen, so it never comes back right in front of you
- Trees past the hero stay until the hero is about to pass them
- Any other tree in the way of the hero still goes

if-high.author: claude
if-high.caption: The same with the default, high camera.

if-low.author: claude
if-low.caption: Walking the trail with the camera low behind the hero, at three points: Line to hero, Lower middle, and In front (now). In front keeps the trees ahead and clears the view to the hero.

if-numbers.author: claude
if-numbers.text:
# Walking the trail, low and high
The same walk along the trail in each way, counting every frame:
- **Trees cut past the hero:** Lower middle 2.2 a frame; In front and Line to hero 0.02
- **Trees near the camera coming back into view:** Lower middle 4 to 7 on the walk; In front 0 to 1
- **Trees reaching into the camera:** Line to hero 0.16 a frame; In front none

It runs as fast as Lower middle, 2 ms faster than Line to hero at the start.

if-ref-center.author: claude
if-ref-center.caption: Your shot with Lower middle: too many of the trees ahead are gone.

if-ref-hero.author: claude
if-ref-hero.caption: Your shot with Line to hero: the branches round the camera pop into the screen.

if-switches.author: claude
if-switches.text:
# To try in F2
Under **Trees in the way**: **In front**, **Lower middle**, **Line to hero** or **Keep**. For In front, two sliders:
- **near camera:** trees whose leaves come within this share of the way from the camera to the hero go (40%, 8 m at the default camera)
- **ahead of hero:** trees past the hero go once it's this close to passing them (1 m)

iw-about.author: claude
iw-about.text:
# Trees go once they're in the way
You said the trees disappeared a bit early, even before the hero reached them, and should only go once some part of them is between the camera and the hero.

Now:
- A tree goes once one of its leaf cards, branches or its trunk is on a line from the camera to the hero, tested against the tree's own shape as it's drawn
- Trees the hero walks towards stay until they're between the hero and the camera
- No more clearing round the hero: the 3 m ring is gone, and so is the mockups' fade of the trees near a high camera. Both can be turned back on in F2 ("clear round the hero", "Fade trees near camera")
- Only what the camera is about to touch, within about 2.5 m of it, still fades

iw-low.author: claude
iw-low.caption: Low cameras: nothing hidden, the previous version, and now. Only the trees that cover the hero go; in the last row the birch goes because one of its branches crosses in front of the hero.

iw-numbers.author: claude
iw-numbers.text:
# How early, before and now
Walking up to a tree from the default camera, it went:
- **Scots pine:** 5 m before its trunk; now 1.5 m, as its branches reach the hero
- **Norway spruce:** 7 m before; now 2.5 m, as its low branches reach over the hero

At 24 random spots and camera angles, trees covered at most 1% of the hero. A few went up to a metre early, from the see-through parts of their leaf cards.

**Speed:** the trees round the hero are drawn now, so the start runs at 51 fps instead of 54; walking the trail averages 65.

iw-pine.author: claude
iw-pine.caption: 3 m before the pine. Before, a clearing round the hero; now the pine and the trees round the hero stay, and the hero is in full view.

iw-walk.author: claude
iw-walk.caption: Walking up to the Scots pine and past it, from the default camera. Before (top) it went 5 m early, with everything round the hero; now (bottom) it stays until the hero is behind it.

lv-about.author: claude
lv-about.text:
# Hiding in the leaves
Your idea, as the new default (Trunk in F2):
- **Trunks:** a tree goes to its stump only once its trunk is in front of the hero, found the way Line finds trees in the way, but against each tree's own bare trunk instead of its whole shape
- **Leaves stay:** leaves and branches in front of the hero don't take a tree, so the hero can stand hidden under a spruce or a crown
- **Deep in the forest:** once the hero is behind the leaves of three trees or more, counted along lines from the camera to the hero's middle, the cone fades in over a quarter of a second and shows the hero through all of them; once the hero is out of the thick of them, it goes almost at once, in a fifth of a second

Walking the trail with the default camera, the hero was behind one tree's leaves a quarter of the time and three or more 5% of it: the cone came on twice, for 0.9 and 1.9 s, and two trees went to their stumps. With the camera low, three or more 17% of the time: the cone came on 5 times, for 0.2 to 5.7 s, and 10 trees went to stumps.

lv-high.author: claude
lv-high.caption: Walking the trail with the default, high camera: Line to hero, Cone, and Trunk (now). With Trunk, the leaves in front of the hero stay (top and bottom rows) until it's behind three trees' leaves (middle row), when the cone comes on.

lv-low.author: claude
lv-low.caption: The same with the camera low, where the hero is behind three trees' leaves or more at all three spots. In the top row the cone is still fading in, a moment after the hero got behind the third.

lv-spruce.author: claude
lv-spruce.caption: Walking in behind a big spruce (2.5 m past its trunk), from 7 m to its side to straight behind it. Trunk (top): its leaves stay, and the hero hides under them, until the hero is straight behind its trunk, when it goes to its stump. The cone (bottom), for comparison, thins it round the hero all the way.

lv-switches.author: claude
lv-switches.text:
# To try in F2
Under **Trees in the way**: **Trunk** (now), or **Cone**, **Front**, **X-ray**, **Area**, **Line** and **Keep**. **trunk: cone behind** sets how many trees' leaves bring the cone in (3 now; 1 brings it in behind any leaves), and **trunk: cone fades out** how long it takes to go once the hero is out of them (0.1 s now, after a tenth of a second). The cone's sliders work here too.

At the start Trunk runs as fast as cutting nothing, 86 fps, 0.7 ms a frame faster than the cone, as the cone is off there. At 12 random spots, each tree that went to its stump would have covered 38 to 99% of the hero; where only leaves were in front of it, they covered up to 56% of it.

m-aim.author: claude
m-aim.text:
# Aim with the mouse
- The mouse aims, separately from movement
- Attacks go toward the cursor
- You can keep moving with WASD while attacking

m-anim.author: claude
m-anim.text:
# What this means for animation
- **Not attacking:** a normal forward walk and run are enough, since the character faces where it goes
- **Attacking:** it faces the cursor but can move any way, so it needs slower walks forward, backward and strafing left and right
- Attacks have to play while walking, which usually means the upper body attacks while the legs walk on their own (layered animation)

m-camera.author: claude
m-camera.text:
# Camera
- Default: a 3D world seen from above at an isometric angle
- Hold the right mouse button to orbit it around the hero, from straight down to low behind (see Camera control)

m-diagram.author: claude
m-diagram.caption: Left: moving normally, the character faces where it goes. Right: while attacking, it faces the cursor and moves slower.

m-facing.author: claude
m-facing.text:
# Facing
- **Not attacking:** the character faces the way it's moving
- **Attacking:** it turns to face the mouse cursor, while you keep moving with WASD

m-move.author: claude
m-move.text:
# Move with WASD
- W, A, S and D move the character
- Holding two keys walks diagonally
- Assumed: directions follow the camera, so W walks away from the camera and A to its left

m-playtest.author: claude
m-playtest.text:
# Tune in a playtest
We'll set these by feel once there's something playable:
- How much slower moving while attacking is
- How fast the character turns to the cursor when an attack starts
- How soon it turns back after you stop attacking

m-questions.author: claude
m-questions.text:
# Open questions on controls
- What does left click do: a basic attack?
- Which keys use skills: 1–4, Q/E/R, or something else?
- Is there a dodge or dash, and on which key?
- Should a gamepad work too (left stick moves, right stick aims)?

m-slow.author: claude

# Slower while attacking
**Important:** moving while attacking is slower than moving normally.

How much slower is still open (see the questions below).

pc-about.author: claude
pc-about.text:
# Path colours and speed
You asked for:
- shadows that stay, only less detailed, instead of a shorter shadow distance
- levels of ground detail between all and none
- path colours with more contrast than the light tan, from darker brown to sandy, that fit a Swedish forest

In the demo, **P** cycles through the seven path colours, and **F2** opens the performance panel with the new shadow and ground options.

Each colour below shows the default camera on the left and a forest close-up on the right. Mark the ones you like with Want, Maybe or Avoid.

pc-ground.author: claude
pc-ground.text:
# Ground details
The ground shader comes in four levels now, each compiled on its own, so a lower level doesn't pay for what it skips:
- **High:** everything, as before
- **Medium:** no flat stones, grit or bumps, and simpler stone outlines. It looks almost the same, and is 4.6 ms faster
- **Low:** the small stones and the leaves only, 4.7 ms faster
- **Off:** 5.0 ms faster

I suggest Medium: nearly all of Off's speed, and the paths keep their gravel and leaves.

pc-iron-soil.author: claude
pc-iron-soil.caption: Iron soil: warm, rusty brown soil, as where the ground is rich in iron, with grey granite stones.

pc-sandy-mixed.caption: Sandy, mixed stones: the light tan paths' sandy dirt, with stones of mixed browns and greys standing out from it.

pc-shadow-options.caption: Shadow options round the hero at the start: fixed at 20 m, the shadows near the hero go; at a lower resolution they stay, only softer.

pc-shadows.author: claude
pc-shadows.text:
# Shadows
**Why they went:** the shadow distance counts from the camera, not the hero, and the camera is 20 m from the hero. Set below about 35 m, it cuts shadows at the top of the screen; below about 25 m, the ones round the hero go.

**Now:** by default the distance fits the view, reaching just past the top of the screen, so it never cuts the shadows you can see. That is 2 ms faster than the old fixed 70 m.

**Less detailed, not fewer:**
- Shadow resolution 1024: softer edges, every shadow kept, 4.8 ms faster
- 512: blurrier, and gaps start to show
- Tree shadows from the far trees: simpler crowns, 4 ms faster

Times are per frame on this laptop's graphics card.

pd-about.author: claude
pd-about.text:
# Play demo (Godot)
A small part of Storskogen to walk in Godot 4.7, about 155 × 110 m:
- **Thicket:** dense pine and spruce like Tätskogen, with a winding trail and a fork
- **Meadow:** open grass like Stora ängen, with lone trees, boulders and a low rise to walk up
- **Same place, two versions:** the mockups' trees or your new portfolio trees, on the same spots. Pick on the start screen; **T** swaps them in the game
- **Hero:** a grey box. WASD walks relative to the camera, right mouse orbits, the wheel zooms
- **The rest is the mockups' own:** rocks, bushes, grass and ground, exported from Blender; the ground shader is ported to Godot

Run it with `godot --path game` (see `game/README.md`).

- Walking speed 5.5 m/s
- **Left mouse held:** stands in for attacking. The hero faces the cursor and walks at 55% speed
- **Camera:** the wheel zooms from 7 to 34 m; the angle goes from 8° to straight down. It stays where you leave it, and the cursor hides while you orbit
- **Trees:** near a high camera they fade out, as in the mockups, and their shadows stay. A hole opens round the hero when trees are in the way
- **Frame rate on this laptop:** old trees 60 fps; new trees 45–60 fps (F4 lowers the render scale)

# How do we see the world?
- **Decided:** a 3D world, seen by default from above at an isometric angle
- **Decided:** hold the right mouse button to orbit the camera (see Camera control)

see-about.author: claude
see-about.text:
# See-through
Your new rule, as the default (See-through in F2), in place of Trunk and its cone:
- **The area:** the hero as the camera sees it and 0.9 m round it (half its height), its corners rounded. Lines from the camera go to a grid of points across it; a point is covered if some tree's leaves, branches or trunk are on its line
- **See-through:** once 30% of it is covered, every tree covering any of it goes evenly see-through, standing on its stump. Over 0.15 s, and back as quickly once it no longer covers any, or the trees cover less than 80% of the 30%
- **No tree goes whole** any more, behind its trunk or not

It's the same dither as the spruces': half the pixels let through, and as every see-through tree lets the same ones through, two in a row are as see-through as one. Deep in the thicket with the camera low, that's most of the screen, and the hero shows faintly: more see-through, or a smaller area, may suit you better.

see-area.author: claude
see-area.caption: Along the trail with the default camera and the area shown: its points red where a tree covers them, its outline red once 30% of them are. The trees covering it go see-through; the rest of the forest stays.

see-birch.author: claude
see-birch.caption: The camera beyond a birch and a young pine, the hero behind them: see-through off (left) and on (right). The birch's stump stays solid at its foot.

see-low.author: claude
see-low.caption: Camera low in the thicket: all of the area covered, and every tree round the hero see-through, the hero faint behind them.

see-switches.author: claude
see-switches.text:
# To try in F2
Under **Trees in the way**: **See-through** (now), or **Cone**, **Front**, **X-ray**, **Area**, **Line** and **Keep**. Then **see-through at** (30%: how much of the area must be covered), **area round hero** (0.9 m), **see-through by** (50%; 0% for never) and **show the area**, which draws it over the view with its points, red where a tree covers them, and how much of it is covered.

Walking the trail with the default camera, the trees covered none of the area two thirds of the time and 30% or more a quarter of it; some were see-through a third of the time (58% with the camera low). The start runs as fast as with nothing hidden; the slowest 5% of the walk's frames 60 fps instead of 70, as what's behind the see-through trees gets drawn too.

sn-about.author: claude
sn-about.text:
# Stumps under see-through trees
You found the see-through trees' stumps hard to see: only their bark stayed solid up to where the stump would be cut, with no top to it. Now a see-through tree stands on its real stump, the same one the earlier ways of cutting trees left, pale cut top and all, and its own bark goes see-through right down to it. The stump stays solid; what's above it, the see-through branches included, lies over its top at half, so the top shows through them.

With **hide all but nearest**, the trees hidden whole now leave nothing but their shadows: no stump, no bare trunk. The one or two kept see-through stand on their stumps.

sn-feet.author: claude
sn-feet.caption: See-through trees on their stumps: a pine, a birch and a spruce, the hero just behind each.

sn-hidden.author: claude
sn-hidden.caption: The slowest low-camera views: all see-through, on their stumps (left); hide all but nearest, the hidden trees leaving nothing (right).

sp-about.author: claude
sp-about.text:
# Play demo: speed
You said the trees and the ground's details on the paths eat the frame rate: about 140 fps without them, 60–80 with one in view, and about 30 with the camera low over many trees. You asked me to find what costs the most and speed it up, with a before and after for each change, so you can judge whether one costs too much of the look.

Now, on this laptop (time per frame on the graphics card):
- **At the start:** 19.3 ms (52 fps) → 10.4 ms (96 fps)
- **Camera low in the forest:** 26 ms (38 fps) → 13.5 ms (74 fps)
- **The meadow path:** 12.3 ms (81 fps) → 5.2 ms (192 fps)
- **Walking the trail:** 65 fps on average → 131, the slowest 1% of frames 42 → 74

sp-changes.author: claude
sp-changes.text:
# What changed, each with its switch in F2
**All as before** and **All on**, at the top of the panel, flip them all at once.
- **Ground details: Baked** (before: High). The stones, grit, fallen leaves and the grass's grain are worked out once at startup into textures, instead of for every pixel. It looks the same and saves up to 6.7 ms on the paths
- **Tree shadows from: Pictures** (before: Mid). A tree's shadow comes from its trunk and branches and one picture of its leaves as the sun sees them, instead of hundreds of leaf cards. Saves 1.8–3.7 ms in the forest
- **Far trees as pictures: 90 m** (before: Never). Trees further off than 90 m are one picture each. Saves 2.5–3.1 ms with the camera low
- **from trees within: 60 m** (before: All). Only trees within 60 m of the camera cast shadows. Saves up to 1.1 ms; at 40 m a big shadow on the meadow goes
- **Leaf cards: Trimmed** (before: Square). The same look, up to 1.7 ms

sp-far.author: claude
sp-far.caption: The far treeline over the rise: always trees (top), and pictures from 90 m (bottom). The pictures look a little fuller than the lightest trees they replace.

sp-ground.author: claude
sp-ground.caption: The meadow path's ground details: High, worked out for every pixel (left), and Baked into textures at startup (right).

sp-more.author: claude
sp-more.text:
# What else costs, and what didn't help
The biggest costs left, at the start (10.4 ms a frame):
- **Shadows:** 2.7 ms, 2.2 of it the trees'
- **Ambient occlusion:** 1.9 ms, up to 3.7 with the camera low
- **Render scale 75%** saves 2.2 ms, and **fewer cards per clump** 2.0, but the crowns get sparser

Not worth it: the lighter trees nearer, a draw distance for the bushes, leaving out the shadows of trees behind the camera (Godot already does), and moving the shadow cascades' split. Without Godot's depth prepass the forest takes twice as long.

Fixed on the way: the Medium and Low ground details worked out High's noise anyway, so they now save a little more.

sp-overall.author: claude
sp-overall.caption: All as before (left) and all on (right), with the panel's new buttons: at the start, with the camera low at the start, and on the meadow path. The numbers are the graphics card's time per frame.

# Tallmo's square

- **Same as the paths:** light tan dirt, gravel in the same tones, fallen leaves, and a worn edge where the grass thins out

st-about.text:
# Trees cut to stumps
You asked for the trees that block the view to go the way Path of Exile 2 does it: cut down to stumps, whenever they're in the lower middle of the screen, the area in your drawing.

Now:
- A tree goes once its trunk crosses that area: the middle 52% of the screen's width, from 30% down to the bottom, and on below it, so trees coming into view from below are stumps already
- What's left is its stump: its own trunk, cut at about knee height, the cut a little tilted, pale wood ringed with sapwood. Its shadow stays
- Any other tree in the way of the hero still goes too
- Beyond the hero, trees go only up to 6 m past it, so a low camera doesn't clear a lane to the horizon

- **Lower middle** (now), **Line to hero** (before: only the trees in the way of the hero, gone whole) or **Keep**
- **Leave:** stumps, or nothing
- **A tree goes by:** its trunk, or any part of it, which also cuts the trees whose crowns reach into the area from the sides
- Sliders for the area's width, how far from the top it starts, and how far past the hero trees go

- **The area's top:** at 30% down, the default camera cuts trees up to about 4 m past the hero

sv-about.author: claude
sv-about.text:
# Worn paths, trees out of the way, frame rate
You asked for:
- the paths in a mix of forest soil and brown earth, with the wear spread further out, so it's less clear exactly where a path goes
- the frame rate not held at 60, or a slider to set it
- trees in the line of sight from the camera to the hero hidden altogether, instead of the round hole

All three are in the demo now; restart it to see them. Mark what you like with Want, Maybe or Avoid.

sv-fps.author: claude
sv-fps.text:
# Frame rate
- VSync held it at 60, the screen's refresh rate. VSync now starts off, with no limit, so it goes as high as the graphics card manages
- **Frame rate limit** in the F2 panel: 30 to 250 fps, or none at the slider's right end
- At the start, on this laptop: 54 fps with the default settings, 69 with Medium ground details, 77 without shadows, 97 with the old trees. Walking the trail averages 68
- The hero still moves 60 times a second and is drawn smoothly in between, so walking stays smooth at any frame rate

sv-panel.author: claude

sv-paths.author: claude

# Paths
- **Forest earth** is a new colour theme, and the demo starts with it: patches of dark forest soil a metre or two across in medium brown earth, with more soil toward the edges. P still cycles through the others
- **Path wear spread** in the F2 panel sets how far the wear reaches: 0 as before, 1 the furthest and the new default. The trampled grass, bare patches and stray stones reach about twice as far into the grass, and break up in patches
- The middle stays a clear gravel path, so you can still follow it

- In the F2 panel: **Trees in the way** (Hide or Keep), and how much ground round the hero to keep clear, 0 to 8 m
- Hidden trees aren't drawn, so hiding them costs the graphics card nothing; finding them takes 0.1 to 0.3 ms a frame

# Tree editor

**Save settings** keeps them; tell me when you have, and I'll rebuild the portfolio and its renders from them.

tp-notes.author: claude
tp-notes.text:
# Notes and open questions
- Heights are about 70% of real trees, so the high camera still sees the ground
- The spruce is the heaviest, about 1,800 leaf cards; a big forest would need lighter versions far from the camera

tr-about.author: claude
tr-about.text:
# Trunks stay, and an x-ray to try
Your front2 shot still had the pine as a stump. That was the rule for trees near the camera: it measured a tree by balls round its trunk as wide as its crown, about 7 m across for this pine, so it seemed near the camera when its needles were 10 m off; and a tree gone near the camera stayed gone while it was on the screen.

Now, from your two ideas:
- **Trunks stay:** a tree in front of the hero loses its crown and branches but leaves its bare trunk, until the trunk itself hides the hero, when it goes down to its stump. Spruces, whose branches reach the ground, go straight to their stumps
- **Near the camera**, whatever of a tree comes close fades away pixel by pixel, trunk kept, so no whole tree goes or comes back there
- **The x-ray** (F2, X-ray): no tree goes whole; a soft-edged window in the lower middle of the screen cuts away what's in front of the hero

tr-switches.author: claude
tr-switches.text:
# To try in F2
Under **Trees in the way**: **In front** (now), **X-ray**, **Lower mid**, **Line** or **Keep**; and **leave**: **Trunks** (now), **Stumps** or **Nothing**. **near the camera** sets how far the fade near the camera reaches.

In front with trunks runs about 1 ms faster than Line at the start; the x-ray, which cuts no tree whole, 2.6 ms slower than In front.

vl-about.author: claude
vl-about.text:
# See-through spruces
For when a single spruce hides the hero, short of the three trees' leaves the cone needs: while spruces' needles cover most of the hero (half the lines from the camera to its middle or more), those spruces go evenly see-through, so you see the hero and the spruce at once. They go over 0.15 s, and come back as quickly once the hero is out from behind them. The trunk rule still comes first: straight behind a spruce's trunk, it goes to its stump.

It's the cone's fine dither, evenly over the whole tree: half its pixels let through what's behind it, however many layers of needles there are. Blending them instead would stack up over the overlapping needle cards and stay nearly solid in the middle.

Other trees' leaves still hide the hero, as you asked: theirs are thinner, with gaps. Walking the trail, a spruce was see-through 16% of the time with the default camera, 31% with the camera low.

In F2, under Trees in the way: **spruce covers** (50%) sets how much of the hero spruces must cover, and **spruce see-through** (50%) how see-through they go; 0% turns it off.

welcome.author: claude
welcome.text:
# How to use this board
- Add notes, images, video clips, links and color swatches with the buttons up top, or drop and paste them anywhere
- Mark anything **Want**, **Maybe** or **Avoid** so we agree on what fits and what doesn't
- Each section has starter questions. Answer them, edit them, delete them, or add sections of your own
- I read this board before we plan, so the more that's here, the closer the game gets to what you picture

wp-about.author: claude
wp-about.text:
# Worn paths
Paths are worn into the grass by feet, so they no longer end in a hard line:
- **Edges:** the grass thins out in ragged clumps toward the path, and the grass along it is drier and trampled
- **Gravel:** small flat stones of mixed sizes on packed dirt, densest in the middle, with a few kicked out into the grass
- **Props:** low grass tufts and pebbles along the edges break up the outline
- **Also:** roads now show through meadows and the town, where the meadow grass used to cover them, and the needle litter under trees fades out instead of ending in a zigzag

With the gravel showing, the paths read a little greyer. The mix of dirt and gravel is easy to tune.

wp-game.author: claude
wp-game.text:
# In the game
- The terrain shader needs each spot's distance to the nearest path, from a path mask painted or generated over the terrain
- Gravel can be a tiling texture with a normal map, blended in by that distance
- Tufts and pebbles along the edges can be scattered from the same mask

wp2-about.author: claude
wp2-about.text:
# Worn paths, version 2
- **Lighter paths:** light tan dirt, between wheat and desert sand
- **Stones blend in:** the gravel and pebbles are the same tones as the dirt, so they read as texture rather than grey spots
- **Fallen leaves:** small yellow, orange and brown leaves on the grass and the paths, thicker in loose drifts
- **Grass under the trees:** the brown needle litter is gone, so the grass runs right up to the trunks
